newsitem.title: FRANCE: French communists to join Jospin government.
newsitem.headline: French communists to join Jospin government.

text.p: The French Communist Party said on Wednesday it would particpate in the Socialist-led government of Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, making official a recommendation on Tuesday by the party's national leadership.

The party said its national leader, Robert Hue, would not take a ministerial portfolio in the new government. The Communists hold the balance of power after a Socialist-led victory in Sunday's National Assembly election.

The Communists were expected to be given two ministries and one junior ministerial post in the new left-wing government. Socialist party sources said Jospin would name his new government Wednesday evening or Thursday morning.
The Communists were last in government under late President Francois Mitterrand, from 1981-84. They held the balance of power when a Socialist-led government ruled from 1988 to 1993.

The Socialists and Communists signed a pre-election declaration outlining plans to cut the working week to 35 hours from 39 and to create 700,000 youth jobs. But the Communists want both measures implemented far faster than the Socialists.
The Communist party won 38 of 577 National Assembly seats in Sunday's parliamentary election. The non-Communist left won 274 seats -- short of the 289 needed for a majority.
